newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index up on special boards.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index up on special boards.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index gained 17.83 points to close at 3510.07 on Monday, boosted by active trading on the three-day special board, bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 45.788 million shillings on 936,363 shares from 32.444 million shillings on 619,123 shares on Friday.
It was the first time that the index closed beyond the 3,500-mark this month.
Some 500,000 shares of Bamburi Cement were traded at a reserve price of 43 from 40.50 on the three-day offer board. Financial analysts maintain that this remains an attractive buy to foreigners.
"Bamburi has systematically capitalised their reserves so investors are able to buy at relatively low prices for the long term," a senior broker said.

The firm issued a bonus of one share for one in the year ended 1995. Together with East African Portland Cement they are the only manufacturers of cement in the country and also export to neighbouring countries.
Bourse officials said it was a very exciting day, untypical for a Monday. Many heavy transactions pushed prices up supported by continued foreign demand on selected shares.
Foreigners traded Kenya Commercial Bank at between 90 and 90.50 from 90, Uchumi Supermarkets at 40-40.50 from 40 and National Industrial Credit at 49.50-51 from 49.50.

One dealer said the recent price rally seen over the last week marked the beginning of yet another cycle of increases riding on anticipated year-end results -- to be released anytime between end of February and early March.
"The prices are getting closer to where the action is, that is the beginning of March," another broker said.
Nation Printers & Publishers closed at 108 from 107, while Kenya Airways eased to 8.85 from 9.
Standard Chartered Bank closed at 56 from 56.50, Rea Vipingo Plantations eased to close at 12.20 from 12.60.
